title: The Stone That Chooses to Spin One Way: The Stubbornness of the Celt
summary: Describes the boat-shaped celt (rattleback), which, when spun in the wrong direction, begins to wobble on its own and then reverses its direction of spin. The episode shows that this phenomenon does not violate the conservation of angular momentum. A small angular offset between the body's axes of curvature and its mass axes transfers energy between rocking and spinning, and friction against the table surface mediates this transfer. The episode also traces the line of work running from George Walker's first analysis in eighteen ninety-six to Hermann Bondi's treatment in nineteen eighty-six and later studies of chaotic behavior.
